part_title: Amazon SQS Fundamentals and Queue Consumers

scenes.title: Amazon SQS: What Is a Queue?
scenes.narration: Amazon Simple Queue Service provides a durable message buffer between producers and consumers. A producer sends a message without waiting for downstream processing to finish, and a consumer retrieves work when capacity is available. This decouples application tiers and absorbs traffic spikes. A queue is not a database query engine or an event broadcast service: consumers process individual work items. In a generative AI architecture, a web API can enqueue summarization tasks while workers invoke Bedrock asynchronously. Configure visibility timeouts, retention, failure handling and dead-letter queues according to job duration and retry requirements. A useful example is a summarisation endpoint that returns a job ID immediately and lets a separate worker process the SQS message later.

scenes.title: Amazon SQS Standard Queue
scenes.narration: A Standard SQS queue supports high throughput and at-least-once delivery. Messages can occasionally arrive more than once or in a different order than sent, so consumers must be idempotent. Contrast that with FIFO queues where ordering and deduplication controls are available with throughput and design considerations. A successful receive does not remove a message; the consumer explicitly deletes it after processing. If processing fails, visibility timeout expiry makes the message available again. For AI job processing, use stable task identifiers to avoid duplicate costly model invocations and tune concurrency based on service quotas. If an invoice processor writes the same result twice because of duplicate delivery, the design needs an idempotency key rather than a bigger queue.

scenes.title: SQS Producing Messages
scenes.narration: A producer uses SendMessage or a batch API to place a message on a queue. It should include a compact task payload or a secure reference to larger data, such as an S3 object key, rather than embedding full documents. Queue configuration can involve message attributes, retention and server-side encryption. Permissions must authorize the sender's role or account, and cross-account access may require a queue resource policy. Once the message is accepted, the producer can acknowledge the request without knowing exactly when processing will complete. Track a correlation ID that the eventual consumer can use for logging and status. When the task contains a reference to S3, remember the consumer must still have permission to read that object.

scenes.title: SQS Consuming Messages
scenes.narration: Consumers poll SQS for available messages, process each item, then delete only successfully completed messages. Long polling can reduce empty receives and unnecessary API calls. The visibility timeout must be long enough for processing, or extended while a long-running job is active. A failed message should eventually move to a dead-letter queue after the configured receive count, so one poison message does not repeat forever. Lambda event source mappings can invoke consumers in batches and support partial batch failure responses. For Bedrock workloads, bound concurrency and handle throttling rather than retrying every model call immediately. The message is not finished when it is received. A successful delete after durable processing is the decisive step.

scenes.title: SQS with Multiple EC2 Consumers
scenes.narration: Multiple EC2 worker instances can poll the same SQS queue to share a backlog. Each visible message is delivered to an eligible consumer, rather than being broadcast to all workers. Visibility timeouts help prevent concurrent processing in normal operation, but duplicate delivery remains possible. Consumers need the appropriate IAM role, network access and application-level idempotency. Monitor approximate queue depth and age of the oldest message to understand whether processing keeps pace. In an AI batch pipeline, workers can independently process document references, write results to durable storage and delete messages only once the output is committed. With four consumers, a single message is work for one consumer, not a broadcast to all four. SNS would be better for independent fan-out.
